questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Components
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+1\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{21}}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{b\cdot a}{|\,a\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a-{\text{comp}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{21}}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{4\sqrt{6}-4\sqrt{21}}{\sqrt{126}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
questions.problem: Let $p=⟨3,5,x⟩$ and $q=⟨-3,1,2⟩.$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is zero, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =3\cdot (-3)+5\cdot 1+x\cdot 2 \\  & =2x-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 2x-4 & =0 \\ 2x & =4 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =(-1)\cdot 2+2\cdot x+1\cdot 0 \\  & =-2+2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ -2+2x & =0 \\ 2x & =2 \\ x & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
